items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: I'm sure that Bunny and Bix are doing all right too.

ctx.x: I mean, Faby has only very little time left. Mr. Armstrong, this is interesting. Of the American composers today, saying the symphonic theme or an opera, who do you like best?

Even when I was in school, I played all classical music. When I was in the orphanage, we played duets. And that was the music. So that instills the soul in you. You know? Litz, Bach, Bach, Marnonoff, Gustav Mahler, and Haydn. We had a little laugh there, where he kept on saying, Haydn, Haydn. And I said, well, let him come out. You know? That was Haydn's style, too. He'd surprise you any time. Every composer that there was, we used it in this song. I'm glad you mentioned Mahler. He's one of my favorite composers.…

We have been visiting with Mr. Louis Armstrong internationally known New Orleans jazz trumpeter and band leader and his guests Mr. Benny Benack and Dr. Frederick Dorian. items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: musicians like Bix and Paul Whiteburn and all them people sitting down. They couldn't understand how we played so well together.

ctx.x: Well, I stayed with Oliver a long time. See what I mean? After I stayed with Oliver, we got so wedged in together making duets and musicians like Bix and Paul Whiteburn and all them people sitting down. They couldn't understand how we played so well together. When Joe got ready for a break, I had every note to it. And we just sitting right there and didn't say nothing to each other. That's how well I loved them. When did you start recording? When was the first? With Joe Oliver. About 1922. The same time of the…
When you were talking earlier about your playing with Oliver and Kidore, is there somebody now that's playing with you that you expect in the years to come will move to the forefront?
